dataIdInfo.idPurp: This layer is intended as an authoritative consolidation of future land use information within Prince George's County from planning maps created over three decades. It is expected to determine master plan conformance for subdivision applications.
dataIdInfo.idAbs:
This layer contains determinations on preferred future land use (FLU) designation as documented on master, sector and transit district development plans approved by District Council in Prince George’s County Maryland from the early 1990s until the end of 2022. The Planning Department GIS data, Community_Plan_Active_Py, was used to determine which plan map is currently designated as authoritative for any given area. Plan maps were georeferenced and inspected to determine the boundaries of FLU geographies, depicted by tinting, and the intended categorization for each area. Parcels and their boundaries within Prince George’s County were visualized and compared to FLU boundaries as needed to improve accuracy of FLU boundary data by ascertaining intended alignment with these parcel boundaries along with previously created FLU GIS data.

The name of the applicable plan and FLU category was stored as text for each feature, with text matching FLU as printed in the corresponding plan map legend, with exact punctuation and capitalization preserved, resulting in variations in the stored FLU_Plan values for different plans.

FLU_Plan polygons in this layer will generally not overlay areas between parcels such as roadways. FLU_Plan polygons for any parcel or contiguous parcels which are not tinted on the authoritative map will have a null value for the FLU attribute. In cases where a FLU map for the active plan area is unavailable, a polygon with null FLU value has been created for each block of contiguous parcels. The authoritative plan map for a given area is not guaranteed to depict a future land use (via tinting) for all areas within the map boundary. Values assigned as null by GeographIT were combined into the 'unknown' category.

FLU_GENERALIZED is derived by reviewing the FLU_PLAN feature and comparing it to the generalized future land use from the Plan 2035 plan as well as a review of existing plans and documents to conflate future land use categories across pre-2014 plans to land use categories adopted in Plan 2035.

Attribute Accuracy Report: This data layer is designed to record decisions on future land use made by The Maryland-National Capital Parks and Planning Commission beginning in 1990. The FLU attribute in this layer simply duplicates the legend entry corresponding to the tint on the source planning map. In a small number of cases, similar tints or a hatched symbology covering a small area may make the intended FLU value ambiguous. More commonly, an untinted area implies that no FLU determination is available, resulting in a null FLU attribute.

Logical Consistency Report: Since FLU values in this layer exactly match legend entries in their source maps, FLU values which are semantically identical but originate from different plan maps may differ eg. in punctuation/capitalization/spacing. This needs to be considered when designing search strategies or automated search/update processes.

Planning maps are not always strict depictions of mutually exclusive FLU categories for all areas. As a result, in some cases, the FLU_Plan attribute documents an existing natural or manmade feature which has a corresponding legend entry.

Completeness report: As of initial publication, this layer is a record of FLU data from currently existing plans. These plans depict future land use via a tinted map with a delineated boundary. Roadways discernible at the map scale are generally untinted. Consistent with this, parcel gaps aligned with roadways are not covered by the FLU polygons in this data layer. In addition, plan maps may have other areas, within parcel boundaries, that are not tinted. In this case FLU polygons have been created for such parcels or groups of contiguous parcels, with null FLU values.

Positional Accuracy Report: The production process of newer planning maps facilitates highly precise alignment of FLU boundaries with existing parcel boundaries where that is the intent of the planner. Older maps may require analysis and judgement to determine the exact effective location of a given FLU boundary. Scanned paper maps covering large areas may not be amenable to georeferencing with high precision in all areas (without a dense street network), for example near folds in a physical map. Often a FLU boundary clearly mimics an irregular parcel boundary, sometimes determined by a natural feature, which aids a precise interpretation of this boundary. In other cases aerial imagery and ad hoc property research has been used to assist in boundary determination.

Due to the nature of the source material and the varying level of detail in the sources used, this layer should be used as a reference only and not for any legislative purposes. The original community plans from which this data was based are the official legal sources.

dataExt.exDesc: The data applies to properties in Prince George's county, Maryland, excepting Laurel municipality, for which no active plan is defined in the active plans layer.
